column3: Adds the same security question, sudden punishment, and lack of awareness, while widening the alternative to the Hour.
Gives the enacted earth-swallowing of owner, house, and unavailable support; retains both support-collapse and forced-descent readings.
Extends sinking imagery to the moon, a cosmic analogue rather than the focus's punitive scene.
Supplies the closest prior parallel: evil plotting, collapse from foundations, and punishment arriving unperceived.
The immediate continuation adds seizure during movement as a distinct alternative to subsidence or hidden arrival.
Reiterates false security before earth-swallowing and its instability; also preserves the two linked V12 readings.
Confirms that predecessors received punishment from an unperceived direction, without adding the ground image.
Pairs earth-swallowing with collapse from above, making the apparently enclosing world unsafe in both directions.
Adds observers' revised understanding after subsidence: apparent prosperity and safety are not secure guarantees.
Adds a nocturnal form of complacency interrupted by sudden punishment.
The next continuation adds seizure through gradual apprehension, completing the nearby set of threatened modes.
Places earth-swallowing among several deserved modes of seizure and explicitly denies injustice; preserves the support-to-humiliation reading.
Frames the awaited consequence as the precedent of earlier peoples or punishment confronting them.
Adds the no-escape dimension for those disputing the signs.
Closely parallels false security on land, subsidence, an alternative assault from above, and loss of any protector.
Adds continuing doubt until an abruptly arriving Hour or inescapable day of punishment.
Connects refusal of the divine call with inability to escape on earth or find protectors.
Reaffirms that delayed punishment can still arrive suddenly while its targets remain unaware.
Preserves a second environmental reversal, by sea and wind, with no later claim against the outcome.
Contrasts protection of one figure with the evil consequence that surrounded the plotting household.
Restates that none can evade on earth and that no ally or helper remains.
Directly joins evil plotting to severe punishment and to the failure of the plot itself.
Adds that apparent flight across earth does not defeat the outcome and ends in an adverse refuge.
Directly denies that workers of evil can outrun the consequence.
Its certainty and inability to evade reinforce liability only at a general level.
Keeps evil plotting under divine control and sets it beside mountain-scale removal.
Affirms the certainty of the divine promise, with only an indirect link to the threatened outcome.
The wish to be leveled with earth is an after-consequence image, not the focus's warning mechanism.
Offers response to the call as an alternative to painful punishment and unescapability.
Shows supports and attachments severed when punishment is seen.
Preserves obedience, awe, and caution as the contrary path, without specifying the threatened event.
Adds moral non-equivalence: perpetrators of evil cannot presume the standing of believers.
Provides rescue from destruction as a counter-scene, but not a direct account of the focus's threat.
States proportional recompense for evil deeds, grounding the consequence in what was done.
Denies that those who reject can get ahead or escape.
Counters confidence drawn from delay: when punishment arrives it cannot be turned away.
Adds failed ransom, hidden remorse, and equitable judgment after punishment becomes visible.
Preserves repentance and faith as a contrary path after evil action.
Sets a warning against corruption on earth before the ensuing seizure narrative.
The unawareness belongs to a separate household decision and adds no clear account of the focus.
Adds seizure by violent shaking in the dwelling after rejection, a different local mode of collapse.
Mockery of messengers explains a recurring response pattern but not the specific warning.
The linked preparedness scene offers only an oblique contrast to failed escape.
Settlement and authority on earth do not clarify the threatened subsidence or surprise.
The call to inspect earth and creation gives a distant reflective frame only.
Inherited dwelling in the garden supplies a reward-side contrast, not the warning's mechanism.
Adds a vertical reversal through Pharaoh's casting into water, parallel to the loss of elevated security.
Links criminal plotting with humiliation and severe punishment, but lacks the focus's security or surprise pattern.
Gathering on earth offers only a broad destination frame.
General divine awareness adds no distinctive connection to the threatened act.
Persistent intention to transgress contributes only a remote moral antecedent.
Names the central error directly: feeling secure from the divine plan is itself ruinous.
Adds a related withdrawal of a life-sustaining resource into the ground, making reliance on stable access precarious.
Adds punishment without relief or aid as the endpoint of an exchanged allegiance.
Self-reproach is a distant inward counterpart to later recognition of fault.
Forbids corruption on earth, but contributes no further account of the focused consequence.
Links failure to recognize signs with inner blindness, a limited angle on being unaware.
Preserves involuntary submission as a secondary vertical-reading context alongside voluntary submission.
Reiterates the compact formula of sudden arrival while targets are unaware, with no new mechanism.
Pairs their plot with a counter-plan operating beyond their awareness.
Adds repeated calamity near homes because of what was done until the promise arrives.
Shows fortified security failing through an unanticipated divine approach and self-ruined houses.
Turns warning before sudden, unperceived punishment into an explicit response opportunity.
The unexpected source here is provision, a contrary use that only sharpens the phrase's openness.
Adds the emergence of an unreckoned consequence and the insufficiency of total ransom.
Exposes earlier confidence in permanence as delusion when punishment arrives.
Legal sanctions for violent corruption are not a close account of this warning's divine seizure.
States that plotters ultimately plot against themselves without realizing it.
Makes the evil plot recoil upon its own makers and invokes the unchanging pattern of earlier peoples.
Adds concealed regret once punishment is seen and locates plot within an oppressive social relation.
The unseen source of temptation is only a lexical contrast to punishment from an unknown direction.
Gives a nearby threatened punishment conditional on violating a sign.
Adds constricted earth and the conclusion that there is no refuge except with God, preserving a repentant reversal.
Denies any safe escape or successful distance from punishment to those relying on false appearance.
States severe punishment without adding its cause, mode, or surprise.
Places all creation in submission and retains the contrary case on whom punishment is due.
A correction of death-related counterfactuals does not clarify the focus's warning.
Describes distortion and disgrace under divine testing, with only a broad punishment connection.
Shows compounded social wrongdoing and punishment, but no close link to plotting or hidden seizure.
Divine predominance despite human unawareness is a distant narrative analogue.
Links turning away from signs to severe punishment, adding a rejection-response frame.
The certainty of promise and the Hour is not a distinct contribution to this threat.
The earlier warning to Thamud supplies the sign and threatened painful punishment behind the later outcome.
Testament procedure during travel has no material connection.
Marriage and penalty provisions do not illuminate the focus.
Covenant failure and deviation give only a general moral counterpart.
Debt documentation does not add to the warning.
Personal burden and earned consequence give only an abstract accountability frame.
Purification rules are unrelated to the focus.
The question about disbelief supplies only a minimal contrary-response context.
A change of people after apostasy is too remote from the threatened seizure.
General divine knowledge does not specify the focus's pattern.
Night practice, travel, and charity do not clarify the warning.
Shows invoked protectors failing when the divine command arrives, extending the loss-of-support theme.
Rules of modesty are unrelated to the focus.
The scattering of graves offers a remote earth-disruption image without the focus's setting.
Knowledge of what is hidden does not itself add the warning's event or relation.
The worship command supplies no distinctive connection.
The tree description has no interpretive value here.
The isolated letters provide no usable connection.
Adds destroyed towns overtaken at night or while at midday rest, directly expanding the focus's unperceived arrival.
Completes the immediate town-security sequence with daytime punishment during play.
Adds that former inhabitants could be struck for their sins, linking historical destruction to moral cause.
Uses a night-or-day reversal of apparent flourishing into devastation, a close analogue for sudden loss of security.
Challenges delayed belief once punishment has already fallen.
Adds an overturned settlement and assault from above, preserving both downward reversal and external punishment.
Generalizes the severe, painful seizure of wrongdoing towns.
Supplies the shadow-based voluntary and involuntary submission context for the secondary focus reading.
Places worldly punishment before the greater later punishment, with no defender available.
Adds a dawn seizure by the cry, a concrete sudden mode of punishment.
Complements that seizure with an upside-down reversal and stones from above.
Directly supplies the later shadow-and-prostration scene underlying the retained secondary reading.
Extends the same nearby submission scene to creatures and angels without pride.
Adds fear of the authority above, but only as a contextual continuation of the secondary reading.
Shows a secure, tranquil town losing its provision and safety after rejection.
The same local sequence states that punishment seized a people while they persisted in wrongdoing.
Sea distress briefly reverses confidence, but the setting is only a loose counterpoint.
Shows a suddenly encompassed possession collapsing beyond recovery.
Makes the loss-of-support point explicit: no faction could help and the owner could not defend himself.
Adds the destruction of an unjust town and its people.
Shows futile flight when the force of punishment is sensed.
States that the event comes suddenly, confounds its targets, and cannot be repelled.
Adds delayed but eventual taking of wrongdoing towns.
Directly follows the listed plot/counter-plot with the destructive outcome of their plotting.
Adds their ruined dwellings because of wrongdoing, giving a built-security counterpart to collapse.
Adds destruction of complacently prosperous towns and the emptiness left after them.
Invokes earlier peoples whose greater strength did not prevent their destruction.
Links corruption on land and sea to human deeds and to a corrective consequence.
Adds a settled, protected landscape reversed into loss after turning away.
Recalls the destructive outcomes of earlier, stronger plotters and denies evasion within heaven or earth.
Shows evil deeds becoming manifest and the mocked consequence enclosing their doers.
Applies the evil-consequence pattern to later wrongdoers as well as those before them.
Calls attention to stronger predecessors whom their gains did not protect from seizure for sins.
Reiterates that prior strength and acquisition did not prevent the realized consequence.
Adds a disgraceful destructive wind as another mode of worldly punishment.
Gives Pharaoh's people as a historical seizure ending in drowning.
Adds a divinely commanded wind leaving former dwellings empty.
Directs attention to prior destroyings and their consequences.
Adds the overturned cities as a concentrated image of total spatial reversal.
Adds their being covered over after the overturning.
Adds a stone-bearing storm as a close above-directed alternative to earth-swallowing.
Names warning of seizure and the refusal that disputes it.
Adds a settled morning punishment after warning.
Completes the immediate 67:16 parallel with danger from above and the reality of warning.
Adds a loss that comes upon a secure garden while its owners sleep.
Generalizes that worldly punishment can be greater still, without collapsing the later consequence into it.
Joins wrongdoing to drowning, fire, and the absence of helpers other than God.
Adds an overwhelming punitive scourge within the historical destruction sequence.
